name: TX-01
label: Safe R

key_factors: Incumbent Moran well-funded with no outside opposition
model.rationale: This east Texas seat is heavily Republican, and first-term incumbent Nathaniel Moran has a large financial edge while Democrat Yolanda Prince has raised almost nothing. With no competitive polling or expert attention, fundamentals and markets both point to a safe Republican hold.
model.watch: A surprise scandal or major outside spending against Moran is the only realistic path to narrowing this race.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
TX-01 is a solidly Republican northeast Texas district with a partisan lean of about 24 points toward the GOP. Nathaniel Moran, the incumbent, is running for reelection after easily securing his party's nomination. He has raised roughly $1.8 million and holds over $775,000 in cash, with no outside groups spending against him.

Democrat Yolanda Prince faces steep odds, having raised under $10,000 with almost no cash on hand and no outside support. Prediction markets give Republicans about a 97% chance of holding the seat. With no public polling and no expert ratings flagging the race, the evidence points to a comfortable Republican win.
